newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels posts net loss, blames "unlucky" June.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels posts net loss, blames "unlucky" June.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. on Tuesday reported a net loss of $3.2 million in the second quarter, citing a run of bad luck at its Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City.
But the loss was an improvement over the year-ago quarter, when the company recorded $44.4 million in red ink resulting from several acquisitions and new casino openings.

The company reported a net loss of 14 cents a share in this year's second quarter, compared with a loss of $2.06 per share in the year-ago period. Revenues for the second quarter rose to $368 million from $235.1 million a year ago.
The company attributed the latest loss to "low table game win percentages" from its gamimg tables at the huge Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, N.J.
Bruce McKee, senior vice president of corporate finance, said the percentage of game wins at the Taj Mahal fell below the industry average of 15.5 percent, to 13.5 percent in June.
"We're basically trying to say we played a little unlucky in June," McKee said in an interview.
That bad luck caused the company to earn $4.9 million less than it had projected in June alone, McKee said. Nearly three-fourths of that shortfall -- $3.4 million -- came from the Taj Mahal.
The results came in well below analysts' expectations of a net loss of 1 cent per share.

Revenues at the Taj Mahal rose to $147 million in the second quarter, from $140.8 million a year ago. Trump Plaza, also in Atlantic City, had revenues of $109.5 million, compared with $106.4 million in the second quarter of 1996.
The company's stock fell 19 cents to $10.56 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
